subject: Private deployment: operator access, audit window & license redlines
messages:
From: Emily Reed <emily.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment redlines (MSA + Order Form) — operator access, audit & escrow-lite

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. I've attached our redlines to the MSA and a revised Order Form (redlined_MSA_Acme_v3.pdf, OrderForm_ACME_v2.docx). A few open items we want to confirm before legal spins up a full review:

- Operator access: We need a clear boundary on what Redwood operators can do in our VPC/private deployment. Specifically: read-only console vs. runbook-driven ephemeral sessions, and any ability to transfer snapshots.
- Audit / evidence: for HIPAA compliance we need an agreed audit window and evidence set (console logs, KV cache access records, snapshot hashes). Are you able to provide an attested transfer process for snapshots (to our S3 with our KMS key)?
- Escrow-lite: we proposed a limited snapshot + runbook escrow model in the redlines — this is not source code, but a snapshot and operator artifacts so we can recover in the event of termination. Please confirm if that scope is acceptable.
- License scope: the draft currently references a "runtime-only" license, but redlines we made call out redistribution limitations and territory. Can Redwood confirm firm language?

We'd like to close these items before routing to procurement. Happy to hop on a short sync — Emily and our security lead can join.

Thanks,
Emily Reed
Director, Cloud Security
Acme Health

---

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Emily Reed <emily.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines (MSA + Order Form) — operator access, audit & escrow-lite

Emily —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the attachments. High level response and proposed approach below; I added Kar and Hannah to loop in legal and compliance.

1) Operator access: Redwood is open to a narrow, auditable operator access model. Our proposed defaults:
   - Scheduled audit windows (pre-booked, "audit sessions") where controlled read-only console access is granted to named Redwood operators for a maximum of 4 hours per session.
   - For maintenance tasks that require write access, we require a runbook and customer approval (signed-off runbook step in ticketing).
   - Emergency break-glass: limited scope (incident response) with full justification, 2-person authorization, and an immediate post-incident report.

2) Snapshot transfer / escrow-lite: we can support a snapshot transfer to customer-owned S3 with encryption under the customer's KMS key; Redwood will provide SHA256 hashes and an audit log of the transfer. For escrow-lite we need to narrow the deliverables to: model checkpoints, runtime container images, and deployment manifests (no developer source tree).

3) License scope: runtime-only license + strict non-redistribution clause is acceptable; legal will propose precise language.

4) Audit evidence: Redwood can provide console audit logs, KV-cache access records, and transfer logs. We do not export low-level host forensic logs by default, but we can include them in a scoped audit if mutually agreed.

Next steps: Kar/hannah will propose contract language for the MSA and a short Order Form addendum for the deployment handoff. Could you confirm two windows per quarter for scheduled audits and whether you need on-demand audits for compliance?

I'll also add a visual diagram of operator access flows (attached operator-access-diagram.png).

— Olga
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Emily Reed <emily.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines — draft redline suggestions

Hi all,

I've reviewed Acme's redlines and here are the legal team's proposed edits we think will get to a pragmatic middle ground without expanding Redwood's operational risk:

- License: Replace your proposed paragraph with the following (suggested contract text):
  "Customer is granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable, runtime-only license to use the Software within Customer-controlled environments for Customer's internal business operations. Customer shall not redistribute, resell, or sublicense the Software outside of Customer's organization without Redwood's prior written consent."

- Operator Access / Audit Window: Contract language we propose:
  "Redwood personnel shall only be granted access to Customer systems pursuant to: (i) pre-scheduled audit sessions not to exceed four (4) hours per session with advance notice of five (5) business days; or (ii) emergency incident response access as described below. All access shall be subject to role-based limitations, time-bound credentials, multifactor authentication, and full session recording and logging. Redwood shall provide a post-access report within three (3) business days summarizing actions taken."

- Emergency access (break-glass):
  "Emergency access may be invoked by Customer via a documented escalation process. Emergency access will be limited to the minimum required scope for incident mitigation, will require two (2) Redwood approvers to proceed, and will trigger an immediate notification to Customer security and a follow-up report detailing scope and duration."

- Escrow-lite: we can agree to deliver a snapshot package upon contract termination or material breach, limited to runtime artifacts (model checkpoints, container images, manifests) and accompanied by transfer logs and crypto-hash verification. Redwood will not provide proprietary developer source code.

- For audit evidence requests outside the standard deliverables, Customer must submit a signed SOC-style questionnaire and cover cost-recovery for forensic-level exports.

I'll include these edits inline in the redlined_MSA_Acme_v3.pdf and push a suggested Order Form addendum for approval.

-Kar
Senior Counsel, Compliance
Redwood Inference

---

From: Emily Reed <emily.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines — emergency access nuance

Thanks Kar and Olga — helpful framing. A couple of clarifications and a possible exception request from our side:

- We accept scheduled audit windows (two per quarter is fine), but our incident response policy requires that vendor engineers be able to perform time-sensitive remediation in the first hour of detection for priority P0 incidents. Can Redwood support a narrower emergency SLA that allows an approved operator to run a limited remediation playbook within the first 60 minutes if the customer security lead confirms verbally? We'd accept a mandatory post-incident forensics packet and a retrospective call.

- Regarding escrow-lite, the only reason we asked for the snapshot + runbook is to support a regulated continuity requirement. We are comfortable with the runtime-only scope you outlined so long as the transfer process uses our KMS and the transfer records are attested.

If you can give a one-paragraph amendment for the emergency SLA window (60-minute initial remediation with customer verbal sign-off, followed by report), we can route to procurement and legal for final sign-off.

Appreciate the collaboration.

Emily

---

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Emily Reed <emily.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines — operator access, audit window & license redlines

Emily —

Thanks — we can accept the 60-minute emergency remediation carveout with a couple of operational guardrails:

- Emergency access limited to named, pre-approved operators; access requires immediate in-band verbal confirmation from the Customer security lead and two Redwood approvers.
- Actions during emergency access must be limited to a pre-agreed remediation playbook; any deviation requires escalation and written follow-up.
- Post-incident report to be delivered within three (3) business days and will include session logs, command transcripts, and transfer hashes where applicable.

Kar will update the MSA with the 60-minute emergency language and a short Order Form addendum that captures the scheduled audit cadence (two per quarter), billing metric (reserved capacity line item and monthly committed units), and the escrow-lite deliverables and process.

Next steps:
- Kar to upload edited MSA and Order Form addendum to the shared Drive (link below).
- Emily / Acme to confirm two preferred quarterly audit windows and share preferred KMS CN for S3 transfer.
- I will kick off a DocuSign envelope once Acme confirms the Order Form numbers; target signature by EOW next week.
